Subject: Staging-only route lock review & operational checklist

Hi team —

Quick ask: MedTech wants their staging environment to be pinned to a single model variant in our staging cluster with explicit no-fallback to hosted variants until they complete their SOC review. They want this enforced for the duration of the pilot (up to 6 weeks) to avoid any accidental cross-region/model fallbacks.

Can infra and product confirm the operational implications and a brief checklist we should share with the customer? Specifically:
- Can we create a policy that pins traffic from MedTech's staging API key to route:staging-pin-medtech (staging-only) and return explicit 503s if the pool is unavailable?
- What will be the impact on autoscaling/burst capacity and SLOs?
- Any monitoring/alerting playbook we should enable (runbooks, escalation paths)?

Attached a rough checklist and a small diagram of the desired routing. Felix from CloudOps is also looped for any infra caveats.

If infra/product can reply with a simple go/no-go + short ops checklist by EOD tomorrow (11 Aug), I can share with MedTech and get their compliance team aligned.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Staging-only route lock review & operational checklist

Kimberly —

Short answer: yes, we can implement a staging-only policy, but there are a few operational trade-offs and a recommended checklist. TL;DR: we should avoid returning 503s to customers quietly (breaks client behaviour); recommend an explicit error response body + dedicated status code that indicates "pinned-model-unavailable" so MedTech can handle it.

Notes / caveats:
1) Policy enforcement: we can create a routing policy named route:staging-pin-medtech that binds API key -> staging pool. If the pool is down we can configure the router to reject (403/409) or return a structured 5xx. Ops prefers a 409 with a canonical error message so we can separate intent from infra failures.

2) Autoscaling & capacity: staging pools are typically smaller and do not get the same burst capacity as dedicated pools. For a 6-week pilot we can set a temporary scaling floor (min 2 instances) and disable cross-cluster bursting. That will raise cost and we'll need an SR to increase capacity if load spikes.

3) Observability/runbooks: enable the following alerts: pool_unavailable, queue_depth_high, kv_cache_miss_rate. Create two runbooks: (A) automated rollback to paused routing (no traffic) and (B) manual escalation to infra on-call. Recommend a test plan (ramp traffic slowly + simulate node loss).

4) Security/compliance: no model or data will leave the staging VPC. However, if MedTech requires cryptographic attestation of the kernel/quantization artifacts, that's a separate ask.

I'll draft a one-page ops checklist. If product wants explicit customer-facing language for the error condition, I can include that.

- Dev
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses — this aligns with our compliance needs. A few clarifications from our side:

- We prefer an explicit, documented error rather than a silent fallback. Our app will show a maintenance screen if it hits that error (so 409 with a defined error code works for us).
- Can we get an SLA for the pilot window that defines expected mean-time-to-recovery for the staging pool (we understand it won't be production SLAs)? Even an internal SLO (e.g., 95% availability for staging pool) helps our compliance reviewers.
- Please confirm that logs for the staging pool (access logs + audit trails) will be retained for 90 days and that we can export them to our Splunk endpoint if requested.

If you can confirm the above and share the ops checklist, we'll lock the pilot and start onboarding next week.

Best,
Nora Li
Security & Compliance, MedTech Health

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below. I'll paste this back to MedTech and add the ticket links.

Decision: APPROVE temporary staging-only route policy for MedTech pilot with the following guardrails.

Operational checklist (short):
- Create routing policy: route:staging-pin-medtech (bind to MedTech staging API key) — Action: Product (Karthik) — target by Mon 16 Aug
- Set scaling floor to 2 instances, disable cross-cluster burst for the pool — Action: Infra (Dev) — will require a capacity SR and cost signoff
- Error handling: return 409 with error_code=pinned_model_unavailable and human message — Action: Infra (Dev) + SDK team to document client behaviour
- Monitoring: enable pool_unavailable, queue_depth_high, kv_cache_miss_rate alerts; add on-call escalation runbook; retention: 90d logs + optional Splunk export — Action: Infra (Dev) + Observability (Lauren)
- Compliance doc: confirm no data leaves staging VPC; provide audit log export steps — Action: Security/Compliance (Lauren)

Open items for MedTech: confirm they can handle 409 client error semantics and accept staging SLO (target 95% availability).

Links: JIRA-INF-1248 (policy creation), https://redwood.app/drive/Shared/staging-route-lock-checklist (ops checklist draft)

I'll mark the ticket as approved pending MedTech acknowledgement. Kimberly — please share the doc with Nora and let me know when they confirm.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Product Manager, Routing & Policies
